payload.question: Did the extra £313,000 councillors voted for get spent on what they voted for?
payload.label: £313,000 for enforcement, communal areas and community clean-ups

target.display: "Investments in enforcement to deliver visible improvements… Communal areas improvements… Community clean-up activity… 313" — Annex C, Budget Council, 24 February 2026

payload.council_caveat: The council built its own check into the promise: "A six-month review will assess progress against KPIs and consider whether targeted community-action pilots… should be incorporated where evidence shows additional benefit."
payload.evidence: Annex C to the Budget Council papers for 24 February 2026 lists £313,000 of extra spending — fly-tipping and graffiti enforcement, bin stores and recycling in flats, community clean-ups, and political assistants — to be funded "in-year from the 2026-2027 budget contingency". The annex says this part "will form part of the substantive motion and not as an amendment", so it was in the budget put to the vote rather than tabled against it. The same annex carries amendments from the other groups that were not part of that motion: £65,000 for a ward-level community cohesion fund from the Green and Liberal Democrat groups, and £45,000 for tree planting and £55,000 for river education from the Green group. No minute of that meeting is in this archive, so we cannot say from here what was finally agreed, or what has been spent since.
